---
A purge keeps the row of a skill that has test cases or a version referenced by a run, a download or a bundle; the deleted-skill sweep also keeps a skill while its publication is unretired or retired less than the ninety-day name hold ago, and while an operator takedown or access restriction is in force on it. An operator can take down or restrict a skill its owner has deleted until the sweep purges it, and the operator's skill search lists such a skill with when it was deleted.

# Relations
- Contexts: [registry](/contexts/registry)

# Examples
- A deleted skill past grace that has test cases survives the sweep.
- A deleted skill whose publication retired 89 days 23 hours ago survives the sweep; at 90 days and a minute it is purged.
- A skill its owner deleted while an operator takedown was in force survives the sweep past grace; after the operator lifts the takedown the next sweep purges it.
- A skill its owner deleted before any complaint is found by the operator's search, taken down or restricted, and then survives the sweep past grace; a deleted skill nobody holds is purged.

---
When a Run's attempt is lost with its provider, the platform asks the model gateway to revoke that attempt's model key before it dispatches the next attempt, so the lost sandbox cannot keep spending on a key the Run no longer uses. A revocation the gateway refuses is counted and left to cleanup, which revokes it again.

# Relations
- Contexts: [run](/contexts/run)

# Examples
- A provider that stops answering mid-run: the attempt ends provider_lost, its key is revoked, and a new attempt receives a new key.
- The gateway is unreachable at revocation time: the reassignment still proceeds and the cleanup pass revokes the key later.

When a credit ledger is configured, a Run is admitted only if the Workspace can reserve the run budget in force when it is created: the operator-set ceiling in run_model_budget_setting, or the deployment's when none is set. The Run keeps that ceiling in its policy snapshot, and its attempts run under it whatever the setting becomes later; a Workspace that cannot reserve it is refused with credit_balance.

# Relations
- Contexts: [run](/contexts/run)

# Examples
- A Workspace with 100 credits is refused with credit_balance under a 0.50 USD ceiling and admitted once the operator lowers it to 0.05 USD.
- A Run created under a 0.05 USD ceiling issues its first gateway key at 0.05 USD after the operator raises the ceiling to 2 USD.
- A deployment with no credit ledger admits the Run without a reservation.

---
A trial Run is admitted only when the gateway's platform-wide model budget, less what is already spent and less the ceiling of every unfinished Run, still covers this Run's ceiling. Otherwise the preflight summary is blocked with platform_model_budget and creating the Run is refused for the same reason: no Run is created and nothing is charged, and the refusal says the budget recovers at 08:00 Taipei time. A budget or count that cannot be read admits the Run, because the gateway still enforces its own budget.

# Relations
- Contexts: [run](/contexts/run)

# Examples
- Limit 50, spent 49.75, nothing in flight, ceiling 0.25: admitted.
- Limit 50, spent 49.5, two Runs in flight, ceiling 0.25: refused.
- The gateway's budget endpoint answers 500: the preflight shows nothing blocked.

    excerpt_sha256: "sha256:50028b9a1a1a887d91aecd4ac6ec84f31a4157c36774b04e8747ea7fdfa1ca7b"
---
When the model gateway refuses a call because its platform-wide budget for the period is spent, the refusal is named as such rather than reported as a broken gateway, and every such refusal is counted for alerting. A creation step refused this way is not counted against the session, the session waits for the person to send again, and only the cost actually incurred is settled; a skill generation or a criteria suggestion refused this way answers 503 saying nothing was charged and that retrying now is refused too; a judgement refused this way settles as failed with a summary naming the spent budget, that it was not charged and that it will be judged again; the evaluation job is snoozed hourly without spending its attempts, and once the budget recovers a new judgement supersedes the failed one, giving up after a bounded number of snoozes. Every such refusal tells the person the budget recovers at 08:00 Taipei time (UTC midnight) each day, which holds only while the gateway's budget period is one day. A refusal of one key's own budget is not this case and stays an ordinary gateway failure.

# Relations
- Contexts: [creation](/contexts/creation)
- Contexts: [ingest](/contexts/ingest)
- Contexts: [testlab](/contexts/testlab)
- Contexts: [eval](/contexts/eval)

# Examples
- The gateway answers 429 budget_exceeded without naming a key: the capability service answers 503 "model gateway platform budget exhausted" and the creation session returns to waiting for input with its step count unchanged.
- The gateway answers 429 budget_exceeded naming the step's key: the capability service answers 502 and the step fails as before.
- A skill generation refused this way answers 503 and creates no version.

files.m/registry/rules/creation-reaches-its-co:
---
type: Business Rule
status: draft
sources:
  - resource: "docs/adr/ADR-016-platform-bounded-contexts-and-context-map.md#L53-53"
    excerpt_sha256: "sha256:5665a77570ab86754c4b5578e93d83c1657f67ffcc095b8bd8e4f5723b6b0c9b"
  - resource: "apps/platform/.golangci.yml#L106-122"
    excerpt_sha256: "sha256:870b6a9c1aff1e2521f150827c6cb1eb887dc6b6b919fdd46d452c91e4793691"
---
Interactive Skill creation does not import the Contexts it collaborates with, and none of them imports it. Everything it needs from the reference, admission and trial Contexts arrives as a narrow interface injected by a composition root, so the creation loop can be replaced or removed without any other Context changing.

# Relations
- Contexts: [creation](/contexts/creation)

# Examples
- Enqueueing a creation job goes through an interface the wiring package supplies, not through the queue Context's own Service.
- A Context that wants to know what a creation session produced reads the Skill Version the session created, not the session.
- Credit and identity are reached the same way every other Context reaches them, because neither is part of the creation loop being kept replaceable.

---
Requesting account deletion starts a 30-day grace period during which the Account stays fully usable; asking again keeps the original request time instead of extending the wait, and cancelling clears the request and is harmless when nothing is pending.

# Relations
- Contexts: [identity](/contexts/identity)

# Examples
- A second DELETE /me keeps the first deletion_requested_at and the same purge_after.
- POST /me/deletion/cancel with nothing pending answers 200 with deletion_requested_at null.
- A fresh request after a cancel starts a new clock with no purge attempt on record.

A dispatch halt declared as a P1 incident outranks a capacity pause on the same target: a later capacity pause replaces neither its source, its reason nor its declarer, and only an operator lifts it. A capacity pause lifts itself after two consecutive clear reconciler rounds.

# Relations
- Contexts: [run](/contexts/run)

# Examples
- The orphan threshold trips while a P1 holds the pool: the halt stays a P1 with the responder's reason.
- A P1 arrives while a capacity pause holds a node: the halt becomes the P1 and names the responder.
- Leaks stay below the threshold for two rounds: the capacity pause lifts, while a P1 on the same target stays.

m/registry/rules/index.md.head:
# Business Rules

- [a-balance-exactly-at-the-start-threshold-may-start](/rules/a-balance-exactly-at-the-start-threshold-may-start) — A start is allowed when the balance is at or above the start threshold; one credit below is refused.
- [a-balance-never-goes-below-the-lowest-stored-balance](/rules/a-balance-never-goes-below-the-lowest-stored-balance) — An entry that would take a balance below MinBalanceCredits is refused with ErrBalanceOutOfRange and nothing is applied; landing exactly on the minimum is appli….
- [a-batch-has-1-to-10-trials-and-1-to-50-distinct-test-cases](/rules/a-batch-has-1-to-10-trials-and-1-to-50-distinct-test-cases) — A batch is refused before anything is saved unless it has 1 to 10 trials and 1 to 50 test cases with no test case repeated.
- [a-batch-is-read-only-within-its-workspace](/rules/a-batch-is-read-only-within-its-workspace) — A batch is read by its id together with the asking Workspace, so another Workspace's batch reads as not found.
- [a-batch-needs-every-test-case-confirmed](/rules/a-batch-needs-every-test-case-confirmed) — A batch is refused as a whole, naming every unconfirmed test case, when any of its test cases lacks confirmed run permissions.
- [a-batch-paused-for-thirty-days-stops](/rules/a-batch-paused-for-thirty-days-stops) — A batch paused for 30 days stops with reason paused_too_long; one paused for less stays paused and can be resumed from its next unrun trial.
- [a-batch-report-is-read-only-under-its-own-skill](/rules/a-batch-report-is-read-only-under-its-own-skill) — A batch report asked for under another Skill of the same Workspace answers not found.
- [a-batch-settles-only-when-no-trial-is-open](/rules/a-batch-settles-only-when-no-trial-is-open) — A batch is marked settled only once none of its trials is still running or owed an answer; a paused batch is neither answered nor settled until it is resumed.
- [a-batch-starts-no-trial-while-dispatch-is-paused](/rules/a-batch-starts-no-trial-while-dispatch-is-paused) — While dispatch is paused for every provider, by an orphan threshold or a P1 incident, an evaluation batch waits instead of creating its next trial, and starts….
- [a-batch-whose-creator-is-gone-stops](/rules/a-batch-whose-creator-is-gone-stops) — When a batch's creator no longer exists, the batch stops as creator_gone instead of starting another trial with no actor.
- [a-batch-whose-test-case-is-gone-stops](/rules/a-batch-whose-test-case-is-gone-stops) — When starting a batch's next trial finds its target gone, the batch stops with reason target_gone and starts no further trial.
- [a-binary-target-gets-no-diff](/rules/a-binary-target-gets-no-diff) — A target file with a NUL byte in its first 8000 bytes is not diffable, so its suggestion is blocked as diff_unavailable rather than applied unseen.
- [a-built-package-is-at-most-the-produced-size-ceiling](/rules/a-built-package-is-at-most-the-produced-size-ceiling) — A package the packager has built is refused when its zip exceeds the produced-size ceiling, and the refusal is counted.
- [a-charge-is-debited-once-per-idempotency-key](/rules/a-charge-is-debited-once-per-idempotency-key) — Replaying a charge under the same idempotency key reports it as existing and leaves one cost event, one ledger entry and one debit.
- [a-charge-needs-a-kind-a-key-and-a-user](/rules/a-charge-needs-a-kind-a-key-and-a-user) — A charge without a kind, an idempotency key or a user is refused as invalid.
- [a-closed-finding-reopens-only-within-30-days](/rules/a-closed-finding-reopens-only-within-30-days) — A new sighting reopens a closed finding only when it was last seen within 30 days; after that it opens a new finding.
- [a-continuation-freezes-a-new-snapshot-for-its-new-prompt](/rules/a-continuation-freezes-a-new-snapshot-for-its-new-prompt) — Continuing a run freezes a new snapshot of the same Test Case whose content hash covers the new prompt, and leaves the earlier snapshot as it was.

---
A search document is listable only once its enrichment is finished or it has an embedding a vector search can find. An enrichment whose embedding call failed is still stored as enriched, without a vector, so it is listable at once; the enrichment backfill later embeds that stored text without calling the enrichment model again, and stores the vector only if the document has not been rewritten since it was claimed.

# Relations
- Contexts: [catalog](/contexts/catalog)

# Examples
- A pending document without a vector is not listable; the same document with a vector is.
- The enrichment answers and the embedding call fails: the document is enriched and listable without a vector; the next backfill pass makes one embedding call and no enrichment call, and a vector computed before a re-import rewrote the document is dropped.

type: Business Rule

  - resource: "apps/platform/internal/creator/workspace/purge.go#L298-314"

    excerpt_sha256: "sha256:c4b66529e4c8621f1fd079b3d377ca3c6eb2786f42c93bc3b4e125ddb0371cea"

---
An account purge starts only when the deletion request is older than the 30-day grace at the moment of claiming and every Run in each of the Account's workspaces has finished cleanup; otherwise the purge is deferred (not failed) and retried by a later sweep.

# Relations
- Contexts: [identity](/contexts/identity)

# Examples
- A request made now is not claimed by a sweep whose cutoff is 30 days ago; the Account does not start purging.
- An Account with a Run still cleaning up its sandbox is skipped this sweep without an error.

    excerpt_sha256: "sha256:587351aa75fd051a0f1e2172d889d9fb455b955927abd7820d707187308779a6"
---
A Run that has reached a terminal status never transitions again. succeeded, failed, cancelled and timed_out have no successors, and a command asking a Run to leave one of them is refused as an illegal transition.

# Relations
- Contexts: [run](/contexts/run)

# Examples
- A cancel arriving after the Run already succeeded is refused, not applied.
- A late provider callback reporting failure on a Run that already timed out is refused, so the recorded outcome does not change after the fact.
- A Run in evaluating may still move to succeeded, failed, cancelled or timed_out, because evaluating is not terminal.

files.hooks/pre-push:
#!/bin/sh
# domain-memory-pre-push
engine='{plugin}/engine'
memory='dm'
existing="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-push.domain-memory-existing" || exit 1
test -n "$DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT" || DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT=$(git config --get domain-memory.git-timeout) || unset DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
export DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
refs=$(cat)
tool_for_hook() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Linux-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/linux-x86_64/domain-memory" ;;
    Darwin-*) tool="$engine/bin/macos-universal/domain-memory" ;;
    MINGW*-x86_64|MSYS*-x86_64|CYGWIN*-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/windows-x86_64/domain-memory.exe" ;;
    *) tool="$engine/target/release/domain-memory" ;;
  esac
  test -x "$tool" && return 0
  echo "domain-memory pre-push: no Domain Memory executable at $tool; build one with cargo build --release --manifest-path $engine/Cargo.toml" >&2
  return 1
}
tool=''
if [ -e "$existing" ]; then
  if [ ! -x "$existing" ]; then
    echo "domain-memory pre-push: the chained hook $existing is not executable, so it would not run; make it executable (chmod +x) or delete it" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$refs" | "$existing" "$@" || exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$refs" | while read local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  test -n "$local_sha" || continue
  test "$local_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" && continue
  range="$local_sha --not --remotes"
  test "$remote_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" || range=$remote_sha..$local_sha
  commits=$(git rev-list $range -- "$memory") || exit 1
  test -n "$commits" || continue
  test -n "$tool" || tool_for_hook || exit 1
  printf '%s\n' "$commits" | "$tool" verify-git-governance --registry-root "$memory" --repo-root . --stdin || exit 1
done || exit 1

#!/bin/sh
# domain-memory-pre-commit
engine='{plugin}/engine'
memory='dm'
existing="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit.domain-memory-existing" || exit 1
test -n "$DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT" || DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT=$(git config --get domain-memory.git-timeout) || unset DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
export DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
tool_for_hook() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Linux-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/linux-x86_64/domain-memory" ;;
    Darwin-*) tool="$engine/bin/macos-universal/domain-memory" ;;
    MINGW*-x86_64|MSYS*-x86_64|CYGWIN*-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/windows-x86_64/domain-memory.exe" ;;
    *) tool="$engine/target/release/domain-memory" ;;
  esac
  test -x "$tool" && return 0
  echo "domain-memory pre-commit: no Domain Memory executable at $tool; build one with cargo build --release --manifest-path $engine/Cargo.toml" >&2
  return 1
}
if [ -e "$existing" ]; then
  if [ ! -x "$existing" ]; then
    echo "domain-memory pre-commit: the chained hook $existing is not executable, so it would not run; make it executable (chmod +x) or delete it" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  "$existing" "$@" || exit 1
fi
changes=$(git -c core.quotepath=false diff --cached --name-status --find-renames --diff-filter=ACMRD) || exit 1
test -n "$changes" || exit 0
staged=$(printf '%s\n' "$changes" | cut -f2- | tr '\t' '\n')
printf '%s\n' "$staged" | while IFS= read -r path; do
  printf '"path": "%s"\nresource: "%s#L\npath: "%s"\npath: %s\n' "$path" "$path" "$path" "$path"
done | git grep -qF --untracked -f - -- "$memory/registry" "$memory/source-map.json"
case $? in
  0) ;;
  1) exit 0 ;;
  *) echo 'domain-memory pre-commit: could not search the Registry for the staged files' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
set --
while IFS= read -r path; do set -- "$@" --path "$path"; done <<EOF
$staged
EOF
tool_for_hook || exit 1
if ! report=$("$tool" verify-evidence --registry-root "$memory" --repo-root . --staged "$@"); then
  test -z "$DOMAIN_MEMORY_HOOK_VERBOSE" || printf '%s\n' "$report" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$changes" | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^R/ { print $2 " is renamed to " $3 " in this commit; run relocate-evidence --from " $2 " --to " $3 }' >&2
  echo "domain-memory pre-commit: a staged file no longer matches what the Registry cites from it; details: verify-evidence --registry-root $memory --repo-root . --staged $* prints the full report, as this hook does when DOMAIN_MEMORY_HOOK_VERBOSE is set" >&2
  exit 1
fi
git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD >/dev/null || exit 0
if ! impact=$("$tool" boundary-impact --registry-root "$memory" --repo-root . --base HEAD); then
  echo 'NOTE: domain-memory pre-commit: boundary-impact against HEAD did not run; the commit goes ahead' >&2
  exit 0
fi
verdict=$(printf '%s\n' "$impact" | sed -n 's/^  "verdict": "\(.*\)",$/\1/p')
test "$verdict" = no-cross-context-change || echo "NOTE: domain-memory pre-commit: boundary-impact against HEAD reports ${verdict:-no verdict}; run boundary-impact --base HEAD to see the Contexts this change touches" >&2
exit 0

#!/bin/sh
# domain-memory-pre-commit
engine='{plugin}/engine'
memory='.'
existing="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit.domain-memory-existing" || exit 1
test -n "$DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT" || DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT=$(git config --get domain-memory.git-timeout) || unset DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
export DOMAIN_MEMORY_GIT_TIMEOUT
tool_for_hook() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Linux-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/linux-x86_64/domain-memory" ;;
    Darwin-*) tool="$engine/bin/macos-universal/domain-memory" ;;
    MINGW*-x86_64|MSYS*-x86_64|CYGWIN*-x86_64) tool="$engine/bin/windows-x86_64/domain-memory.exe" ;;
    *) tool="$engine/target/release/domain-memory" ;;
  esac
  test -x "$tool" && return 0
  echo "domain-memory pre-commit: no Domain Memory executable at $tool; build one with cargo build --release --manifest-path $engine/Cargo.toml" >&2
  return 1
}
if [ -e "$existing" ]; then
  if [ ! -x "$existing" ]; then
    echo "domain-memory pre-commit: the chained hook $existing is not executable, so it would not run; make it executable (chmod +x) or delete it" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  "$existing" "$@" || exit 1
fi
changes=$(git -c core.quotepath=false diff --cached --name-status --find-renames --diff-filter=ACMRD) || exit 1
test -n "$changes" || exit 0
staged=$(printf '%s\n' "$changes" | cut -f2- | tr '\t' '\n')
printf '%s\n' "$staged" | while IFS= read -r path; do
  printf '"path": "%s"\nresource: "%s#L\npath: "%s"\npath: %s\n' "$path" "$path" "$path" "$path"
done | git grep -qF --untracked -f - -- "$memory/registry" "$memory/source-map.json"
case $? in
  0) ;;
  1) exit 0 ;;
  *) echo 'domain-memory pre-commit: could not search the Registry for the staged files' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
set --
while IFS= read -r path; do set -- "$@" --path "$path"; done <<EOF
$staged
EOF
tool_for_hook || exit 1
if ! report=$("$tool" verify-evidence --registry-root "$memory" --repo-root . --staged "$@"); then
  test -z "$DOMAIN_MEMORY_HOOK_VERBOSE" || printf '%s\n' "$report" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$changes" | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^R/ { print $2 " is renamed to " $3 " in this commit; run relocate-evidence --from " $2 " --to " $3 }' >&2
  echo "domain-memory pre-commit: a staged file no longer matches what the Registry cites from it; details: verify-evidence --registry-root $memory --repo-root . --staged $* prints the full report, as this hook does when DOMAIN_MEMORY_HOOK_VERBOSE is set" >&2
  exit 1
fi
git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD >/dev/null || exit 0
if ! impact=$("$tool" boundary-impact --registry-root "$memory" --repo-root . --base HEAD); then
  echo 'NOTE: domain-memory pre-commit: boundary-impact against HEAD did not run; the commit goes ahead' >&2
  exit 0
fi
verdict=$(printf '%s\n' "$impact" | sed -n 's/^  "verdict": "\(.*\)",$/\1/p')
test "$verdict" = no-cross-context-change || echo "NOTE: domain-memory pre-commit: boundary-impact against HEAD reports ${verdict:-no verdict}; run boundary-impact --base HEAD to see the Contexts this change touches" >&2
exit 0
